brief: The birth of Jesus was accompanied by violence, just as the Israelites had suffered violence in Egypt. The baby Jesus had to flee for his life, and in his place Herod the Great, Jewish ruler for 37 years under the Romans, put to death male children two and under in and around Bethlehem. Although we have no other evidence of this massacre, it is consistent with some other acts of Herod. Because these children suffered for Jesus’ sake, the church has regarded them as martyrs.
